fields.meta_title: Refund Request Form Builder for Businesses | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a refund request form that checks each request against your refund policy, sends it for sign-off and keeps the reason on file. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Refund Request Form That Applies Your Policy
fields.hero_description: Describe your refund policy and who approves a refund. Emergent builds the refund request form with the approval steps behind it, and every request lands in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Refund Request Form Needs to Decide
fields.features_subheading: Six parts that turn a customer's request into a clear yes, no or partial refund, with the reason on file.
fields.feature_1:
The order, matched before anyone reads it

Ask for the order number and the email used at checkout. Connect your store, and the app looks up the purchase date and amount. A number with no match goes back to the customer.
fields.feature_2:
Your refund window, applied by date

Write the window into the form, such as 30 days from delivery. Requests inside it go straight to approval. Late ones still arrive, marked with how many days past the window they are.
fields.feature_3:
Reasons as choices, with a note field

Offer fixed reasons such as damaged, wrong item or no longer needed, plus a box for detail. Fixed choices let you count refunds by reason and by product at the end of each month.
fields.feature_4:
Partial refunds worked out on screen

Set the share you pay back by date or condition, like half for a class canceled within a week. The customer sees the dollar amount before submitting, and staff see that figure too.
fields.feature_5:
Sign-off in the order you set

Name who approves each kind of refund and in what order, such as a manager, then finance. Each approver gets an email or a Slack message with the request. Every decision is logged.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Export the form, its approval steps, and the request database to GitHub on paid plans. A developer can wire it into the admin of your store or host it on servers your company runs.

fields.tab_content_1:
Day 9 of 14 is approved on submit

Brightlane sells a writing app on annual plans with a 14-day refund window. Priya Nair asks for her money back on day 9, picking "not what I needed" as the reason. The request is inside the window and is approved on submit. The app refunds her $96 through Stripe. Later requests go to the billing lead.
fields.tab_content_2:
Half back when a seat is canceled 4 days out

Cedar Loft runs weekend pottery workshops at $120 a seat. The studio pays back the full fee 7 or more days before a class, and half the fee inside 7 days. Marcus Bell cancels his Saturday seat on Tuesday, 4 days out. The form shows him $60 before he submits, and the owner approves that amount with one click.
fields.tab_content_3:
No check leaves before the secretary signs

Families who leave Pine Hollow School District can claim a student's unused lunch balance. A parent enters the student ID and a new mailing address. The building secretary confirms the $42.50 balance first. Only then does the request reach the business office, which mails the check and records the date.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each deposit refund starts with the final bill

Every Fallbrook water account opens with a $150 deposit. When a customer closes the account, the refund request asks for the account number and a forwarding address. The app takes the $38.20 final bill out of the deposit and shows the clerk $111.80 to return. The customer gets an email once the clerk approves it.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Refund Request Form
fields.howto_description: Write the policy first. The form is that policy turned into questions, with a named person for every decision it cannot make on its own.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the order number first
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Offer reasons as a short list
fields.howto_step_1_des: Set the window, the reasons you accept, and the cases where you pay back less than the full amount. A policy that lives in one support lead's head treats two identical requests differently. Publish the same text wherever customers pay.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the order or invoice number at the top, with the email used to pay. The purchase date, the amount and the payment method all hang on it. A request without one costs a support agent a search before anyone can decide.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give five or six fixed reasons and one free-text box. Fixed choices can be counted, which shows the product or class behind most refunds. Ask for a photo only when the reason is damage or a wrong item.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Name an approver for each kind of request and the amount above which a second person signs. A school district might need the building secretary and then the business office. A software company might approve anything inside its window with no person involved.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the policy and the approval order into a prompt. Emergent builds the form, the approval steps, and the table each request is saved to. Connect Stripe or your store's admin if approved refunds should be issued from the app.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Show the expected amount and the next step on the confirmation screen, and send both by email. Give each request a reference number the customer can quote if they write in later. Staff find the whole record by that number.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the link goes live, file one request inside the window, one outside it, and one for a partial refund. Check that each reaches the right person with the right amount. Then add the link to your receipts and checkout emails.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is agency PDFs (a Georgia Corporations Division form, a school district's parent form), printable templates (Pinterest, pdfFiller, SampleForms, Forms Workflow) and two template builders. Every one stops at the fields, and People Also Ask is written from the customer's chair: how to ask, which reasons count, whether a reason is needed. This page answers those questions plainly, then shows the side nobody in the top 10 covers: the business deciding the request against its own policy. A software company approves a refund inside its 14-day guarantee and sends it through Stripe, a workshop host refunds half when a seat is canceled 4 days out, a school district needs the building secretary's sign-off before finance mails a check, and a city utility takes the final bill off a deposit before refunding the rest.
